title: HI SCR184: Requesting The Hawaii Civil Rights Commission To Examine The Applicability Of Existing State Anti-discrimination Laws To Algorithmic And Automated Decision Systems.

obligations: The Hawaii Civil Rights Commission is requested to examine the applicability of existing state anti-discrimination laws to algorithmic and automated decision systems (BE IT RESOLVED)

The examination must include an assessment of whether existing state law provides sufficient authority to investigate and remedy discrimination arising from algorithmic or automated determination systems ((1))
The examination must include identification of potential jurisdictional or evidentiary challenges associated with algorithmic discrimination claims ((2))

The examination must include evaluation of whether guidance, rulemaking, or administrative clarification may assist individuals and regulated entities in understanding their rights and responsibilities ((3))
The examination must include consideration of the feasibility of establishing an intake or complaint pathway for alleged algorithmic or automated discrimination under existing state law ((4))
The examination must include recommendations, if any, for legislative action to ensure civil rights and anti-discrimination protections remain effective ((5))

The Hawaii Civil Rights Commission is requested to submit a report of its findings and recommendations, including any proposed legislation, to the Legislature no later than twenty days prior to the convening of the Regular Session of 2027 (BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED)

What it does

This concurrent resolution requests the Hawaii Civil Rights Commission to examine whether existing state anti-discrimination laws apply to algorithmic and automated decision systems. It asks the Commission to assess legal authority, identify challenges, evaluate guidance, consider a complaint pathway, and recommend legislation. It requests a report to the Legislature by twenty days before the 2027 Regular Session.

Who it applies to

  • Hawaii Civil Rights Commission

not stated in the text

  • The Hawaii Civil Rights Commission is requested to examine the applicability of existing state anti-discrimination laws to algorithmic and automated decision systems (BE IT RESOLVED)
  • The examination must include an assessment of whether existing state law provides sufficient authority to investigate and remedy discrimination arising from algorithmic or automated determination systems ((1))
  • The examination must include identification of potential jurisdictional or evidentiary challenges associated with algorithmic discrimination claims ((2))
  • The examination must include evaluation of whether guidance, rulemaking, or administrative clarification may assist individuals and regulated entities in understanding their rights and responsibilities ((3))
  • The examination must include consideration of the feasibility of establishing an intake or complaint pathway for alleged algorithmic or automated discrimination under existing state law ((4))
  • The examination must include recommendations, if any, for legislative action to ensure civil rights and anti-discrimination protections remain effective ((5))
  • The Hawaii Civil Rights Commission is requested to submit a report of its findings and recommendations, including any proposed legislation, to the Legislature no later than twenty days prior to the convening of the Regular Session of 2027 (BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED)

not stated in the text; this resolution does not establish penalties, enforcement authority, or a private right of action.

How it affects AI deployment

  • This resolution does not impose any direct obligations, prohibitions, or penalties on organisations deploying AI. It only requests a study by the Hawaii Civil Rights Commission, which may lead to future guidance or legislation but creates no immediate compliance requirements for AI deployers (BE IT RESOLVED; BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED).

  • Develop recommendations, if any, for legislative action ((5))
  • Submit a report of findings and recommendations, including any proposed legislation, to the Legislature no later than twenty days prior to the convening of the Regular Session of 2027 (BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED)

THE SENATE 
 
 
 S.C.R. NO. 
 
 
 184 
 
 
 
 
 THIRTY-THIRD LEGISLATURE, 2026 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 STATE OF HAWAII 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 

 SENATE CONCURRENT 

 RESOLUTION 

   

   

 requesting the hawai ʻ i civil rights commission to
examine the applicability of existing state anti-discrimination laws to algorithmic
and automated decision systems . 

   

   

   

 

 
 

 

      WHEREAS, Hawaii
has a longstanding commitment to protecting individuals from discrimination in
employment, housing, public accommodations, credit, and access to state and
county services; and 

   

      WHEREAS, the
Hawai ʻ i
Civil Rights Commission is charged with enforcing the State's
anti-discrimination laws and ensuring equal opportunity for all of Hawaii's
residents; and 

   

      WHEREAS, algorithmic
and automated decision systems, including artificial intelligence tools, are
increasingly used in employment screening, tenant selection, credit
determinations, and public benefits eligibility determinations to make
decisions in areas that are traditionally protected by anti-discrimination laws;
and 

   

      WHEREAS, research
and national experience suggests that algorithmic and automated determination
systems may replicate, amplify, or obscure patterns of discrimination,
particularly when these systems are built upon biased data or opaque modeling
practices or lack sufficient oversight; and 

   

      WHEREAS, discrimination
arising from algorithmic and automated decision systems may present novel
jurisdictional, evidentiary, and enforcement questions under the State's
existing civil rights statutes; and 

   

      WHEREAS, ensuring
that civil rights protections remain effective in the face of evolving
technologies is consistent with this body's responsibility to uphold fairness,
equal protection, and public confidence in government; now, therefore, 

   

      BE IT
RESOLVED by the Senate of the Thirty-third Legislature of the State of Hawaii,
Regular Session of 2026, the House of Representatives concurring, that the
Hawai ʻ i
Civil Rights Commission is requested to examine the applicability of existing
state anti-discrimination laws to algorithmic and automated decision systems;
and 

   

      BE IT FURTHER
RESOLVED that the examination include, to the extent possible: 

   

      (1)   An assessment of whether existing state law
provides sufficient authority to investigate and remedy discrimination arising
from algorithmic or automated determination systems; 

   

      (2)   Identification of potential jurisdictional or
evidentiary challenges associated with algorithmic discrimination claims; 

   

      (3)   Evaluation of whether guidance, rulemaking, or
administrative clarification may assist individuals and regulated entities in
understanding their rights and responsibilities; 

   

      (4)   Consideration of the feasibility of
establishing an intake or complaint pathway for alleged algorithmic or
automated discrimination under existing state law; and 

   

      (5)   Recommendations, if any, for legislative
action to ensure civil rights and anti-discrimination protections remain
effective; and 

   

      BE IT FURTHER
RESOLVED that the Hawai ʻ i
Civil Rights Commission is requested to submit a report of its findings and
recommendations, including any proposed legislation, to the Legislature no
later than twenty days prior to the convening of the Regular Session of 2027;
and 

   

      BE IT FURTHER
RESOLVED that certified copies of this Concurrent Resolution be transmitted to the
Chair of the Hawai ʻ i
Civil Rights Commission and Executive Director of the Hawai ʻ i
Civil Rights Commission. 

   

   

   

 
 
 
   
 
 
 OFFERED BY: 
 
 
 _____________________________
